scope: Q10 source verification and form-only SFPL clarification. Does not modify phase-b-q10.json or Phase A.

sfpl.basis: Visible form only: all four are one-sentence Russian technical definitions, all begin with PBT, maintain a professional register, and contain concrete technical claims. Lengths are tightly matched (A 156, B 156, C 154, D 157 characters), so length supplies no useful cue but also does not by itself establish fairness. A/C/D use categorical claims (“позволяет считать”, “доказывает”, “гарантирует”); B uses the more calibrated modal “может”. That hedge can read as more careful and may mildly favor B in tone. However, all options sound like coherent technical explanations and the calibrated wording is natural. Limited conclusion: no formal defect; retain a small style cue note for the softer modality, without treating it as a key giveaway. This assessment does not rely on checking which claims are true.

pinned_source_checks.finding: The guide explicitly says predefined generators never create null; to allow null, call Arbitrary.injectNull(probability). Thus standard List<Integer> generation does not include null absent a null-injection customization.

pinned_source_checks.section: Constraining Default Generation → Allow Null Values
pinned_source_checks.finding: @WithNull injects null into generated values at a configured probability, for generated types. This confirms null requires opt-in.

GenerationMode.AUTO is default and chooses exhaustive generation when sensible relative to tries; RANDOMIZED always uses randomized generators; EXHAUSTIVE uses supported finite enumeration; DATA_DRIVEN consumes @FromData.

ShrinkingMode.BOUNDED is default, tries up to 10 seconds, then reports the best sample at timeout; FULL continues until no smaller falsifying value is found and may take a very long time or rarely fail to terminate. This supports the bounded/strategy-limited caveat, not a global-minimum guarantee.
